hooks.text: For a full century, the heaviest invertebrate on Earth was a ghost.
How do you film an animal that science has only ever seen dead?
After one hundred years of waiting, the colossal squid was finally filmed alive.

title: First live footage of the colossal squid
description: For a century, the colossal squid was known only from dead specimens and whale stomachs. On March 9, 2025, researchers finally filmed a live juvenile in the South Atlantic.

beats.text: For a full century, the heaviest invertebrate on Earth was a ghost.
beats.visual: Colossal squid museum specimen in Te Papa museum, Wellington
queries: Colossal squid specimen Museum of New Zealand

beats.text: Known mostly from damaged dead specimens and whale scars, the colossal squid had never been seen swimming alive anywhere.
beats.visual: Sperm whale diving in the open ocean

beats.text: That incredible dark mystery changed completely on March 9, 2025, near the remote South Sandwich Islands.
beats.visual: South Sandwich Islands landscape and iceberg in the Southern Ocean

beats.text: An international research team using the advanced remotely operated vehicle SuBastian recorded the historic moment.
beats.visual: ROV SuBastian underwater during Schmidt Ocean Institute expedition

beats.text: The camera surprisingly revealed a translucent juvenile measuring about 12 inches long.
beats.visual: Cranchiidae glass squid swimming in the mesopelagic zone

beats.text: It drifted quietly in the dark blue at a depth of 600 meters.
beats.visual: Mesopelagic zone ocean illustration showing deep sea bioluminescence

beats.text: After a full century hidden away as a ghost, the heaviest invertebrate on Earth finally came into focus.
beats.visual: Research vessel Falkor too operating in the Southern Ocean
